root_cause.text: The MPTCP path manager's ADD_ADDR retransmission timer handler uses `__sock_put()` instead of `sock_put()`, failing to free the socket when it holds the last reference, and if `sock_put()` were used, `sk_free()` would deadlock by trying to synchronously stop the same timer that is currently executing.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `__sock_put(sk)` to `sock_put(sk)` and adds a `timer_done` flag set to true when the timer is not rescheduled, so that `mptcp_pm_free_anno_list` avoids calling `sk_stop_timer_sync()` on that timer, preventing the deadlock described in the commit message: "sock_put() will call sk_free(), which will end up calling sk_stop_timer_sync() on the same timer, and waiting indefinitely to finish."

This is the tail of the timer handler declaration (mptcp_pm_add_timer), which is the function that executes the vulnerable __sock_put call. The handler itself creates the context where the deadlock could occur.
Extracts the mptcp_sock from the entry, which is later cast to struct sock and used with __sock_put. This expression is part of the critical refcount manipulation path.
Casts the mptcp_sock to a struct sock, which is then used in __sock_put and other socket operations. This variable carries the reference that is improperly released.
Sets up the per-entry retransmission timer to call mptcp_pm_add_timer. This creates the timing and callback linkage that leads to the recursive deadlock when sk_free tries to stop the same timer.
Synchronously stops the add_timer during cleanup. If sock_put were used and triggered sk_free, this call would attempt to stop the already running timer, causing a deadlock.
